themes.theme: hormuz strait shipping and geopolitical risk
themes.consensus_view: Nine desks treat the Strait of Hormuz shipping chokepoint and the US-Iran talks around reopening it as a live risk this window, but none of them stakes out a directional call on oil or shipping.

facts_agreed.claim: Several banks are tracking US-Iran negotiations over reopening the Strait of Hormuz as the swing factor for the region.
evidence_quotes: Strait of Hormuz shipping negotiations
Strait of Hormuz negotiations
Strait of Hormuz shipping route negotiations
US-Iran negotiations and Strait of Hormuz
US-Iran Strait of Hormuz negotiations

facts_agreed.claim: Banks describe traffic through the strait as still disrupted, with energy flows the channel through which the disruption reaches markets.
evidence_quotes: Strait of Hormuz transit restrictions
Strait of Hormuz shipping standstill
Middle East conflict and Strait of Hormuz traffic
Strait of Hormuz energy supply
US blockade of Iranian ports

facts_agreed.claim: The disruption is being carried beyond the strait itself into wider shipping capacity and oil-services effects.
evidence_quotes: Middle East disruptions in oil services
Red Sea shipping capacity
Iran War oil market disruptions
Strait of Hormuz shipping lane uncertainty

themes.consensus_view: The banks broadly agree the AI buildout is still accelerating and that second-quarter results confirmed it, and the live disagreement is whether spending funded increasingly by borrowing rather than company cash flow can keep driving earnings.

facts_agreed.claim: Second-quarter hyperscaler results confirmed the AI spending cycle is still intact and growing.
evidence_quotes: Hyperscalers’ reports this earnings season reaffirmed that the AI spend cycle remains intact
earnings are solid and the AI capex cycle remains firmly on track
demand and order coverage are improving relative to capex
recent results provide further evidence that AI investment is driving demand
the AI boom has further to run – at least another 12-18 months.

facts_agreed.claim: Planned hyperscaler spending is now large enough to exceed the cash these companies generate, so the buildout has to be part-funded with borrowed money.
evidence_quotes: Consensus estimates imply hyperscaler capex of $1.1 trillion will exceed operating cash flow
more than $1 trillion of hyperscaler capex in 2027 and 2028.

facts_agreed.claim: Demand for AI computing capacity still exceeds what can be supplied, and the spending is pulling through power, networking and software businesses alongside the chips.
evidence_quotes: demand for AI Infrastructure continues to outstrip supply which is a positive for Neocloud players
We continue to see the Reliability investment cycle as durable.
Networking unlocks computing capability for single AI chips, connecting multiple chips, enabling seamless data exchange and low latency.
emergence of potential ‘inference economy’ stocks in Software
recent results provide further evidence that AI investment is driving demand

facts_agreed.claim: AI capital spending is now the main driver of corporate profit growth and overall equity market direction.
evidence_quotes: the AI capex cycle now matters more than the month we’re in.
AI infrastructure spending providing a massive tailwind to corporate profits

facts_contested.claim: whether AI-capex-driven earnings growth is self-sustaining
facts_contested.for_evidence: earnings are solid and the AI capex cycle remains firmly on track
facts_contested.against_evidence: half of the S&P 500's earnings growth is now coming from AI capital expenditure

facts_contested.claim: how much economic damage the AI spending cycle would cause if it reverses
facts_contested.for_evidence: The AI cycle is building at close to twice the pace of the housing boom
facts_contested.against_evidence: our analysis in prior work and above suggests that both claims are exaggerated.

themes.consensus_view: Chip stocks sold off and got dumped by funds through July, and desks now describe them as cheap relative to their own earnings power, but nobody has settled whether that is a buying setup or the front end of a bubble deflating.

facts_agreed.claim: Semiconductors went through a July drawdown marked by fund selling, ETF withdrawals and bearish positioning.
evidence_quotes: Semiconductor sector volatility in July
Semiconductor ETF outflows
Semiconductor sector long position liquidation
Semiconductors & Equipment bearish positioning

facts_agreed.claim: Chip share prices have fallen behind the sector's underlying earnings, leaving room for prices to close the gap.
evidence_quotes: Semiconductor fundamental valuation gap
Semiconductor fundamental catch-up potential
Semiconductor stock rally

facts_agreed.claim: Money that came out of chips moved into software and the largest tech names, where desks see improving earnings.
evidence_quotes: rotation from semis to tech behemoths
Software and Services bullish rotation
Software sector revival
Software earnings AI tailwind
Software and internet sector earnings momentum

facts_agreed.claim: Bank of America points to Applied Materials earnings as the next event that could turn the chip group higher.
evidence_quotes: AMAT could be a positive catalyst for semis

facts_contested.claim: whether the July chip selloff is a recovery entry point or the start of a bubble unwind
facts_contested.for_evidence: AMAT could be a positive catalyst for semis

themes.consensus_view: Money around AI is being repositioned rather than simply added to: funds are putting on new short bets against AI names while keeping their existing long bets, and bonds issued by AI-linked companies now pay more than everyone else's, but the desks split on whether investors are leaving the AI trade or just moving into the biggest names.

facts_agreed.claim: Funds are hedging their existing AI longs by adding shorts rather than by cutting the long positions.
evidence_quotes: The simultaneous short build across both themes, even as long crowding holds near prior levels

facts_agreed.claim: AI-linked borrowers are trading at a wider spread than non-AI borrowers, and that gap is expected to stay wide because the capex funding need is long-dated.
evidence_quotes: AI-driven credit markets are becoming more bifurcated, with spreads of AI-related issuers underperforming
We expect this gap will persist, keeping AI-related spreads wider vs. non-AI peers
our base case for the macro backdrop implies a healthy premium

facts_agreed.claim: Buyers of AI-related debt are getting saturated, with the concentration of AI issuance in the investment-grade market meeting visible resistance.
evidence_quotes: investor appetite is showing clear signs of indigestion.

facts_contested.claim: whether investors are exiting AI exposure outright or rotating within it
facts_contested.for_evidence: investor skepticism – and measures of exposure – to Tech are shifting dramatically.
facts_contested.against_evidence: the bid has shifted up the quality scale as Hyperscalers have seen demand

themes.consensus_view: Banks read the weak July jobs report as a labor market that is cooling and creating fewer jobs rather than one falling apart, and no desk argued the opposite.

facts_agreed.claim: The July payrolls miss shows a labor market that is slowing, not one that is breaking down.
evidence_quotes: consistent with a broadly stable labour market rather than a sharp deterioration
Fed officials have broadly characterized the labor market as stable
it is too early to tell, and would come in the light of a swathe of indicators

facts_agreed.claim: Multiple desks describe US hiring and wage growth as softening over this window.
evidence_quotes: Labor market differential softening
US labor market easing
Labour market sentiment softness
US labor market cooling
US wage growth moderation

facts_agreed.claim: Easing labor market pressure removes the case for further Fed rate increases this year.
evidence_quotes: Our base case remains that the Fed will keep rates unchanged this year.

themes.consensus_view: Six desks agree that second-quarter profit growth beat expectations by a wide margin and that the strength reaches well past the big AI names, so they expect stock gains to spread into cyclical, financial and healthcare shares in the second half, with no bank arguing the other side.

facts_agreed.claim: Second-quarter 2026 profits came in well above expectations and grew faster than the prior quarter.
evidence_quotes: 2Q results continued to track stronger than expectations with Median profits up 17% yoy
Global earnings growth accelerated from an extremely high 26.1% in Q1 to 39.1% in Q2
We remain constructive on equities, supported by strong earnings, broader participation.

facts_agreed.claim: Market gains should spread beyond the largest tech companies in the second half as profit strength shows up outside AI.
evidence_quotes: We expect future gains to come from a broader range of sectors.
We think participation should pick up further in 2H
The building blocks for broader market leadership are emerging

facts_agreed.claim: Buying is already rotating into economically sensitive and non-AI sectors including biotech, housing and financials.
evidence_quotes: buying has broadened into areas like Biotech, Housing, and Financials
we look for Cyclicals to resume leading in 2H, on stronger earnings delivery

themes.consensus_view: Six desks flag the July US consumer and producer price releases as the main scheduled event of the window without staking out a directional call, and the two banks that published numbers land close together at roughly 3.4% to 3.5% headline inflation and about 2.5% underlying inflation.

facts_agreed.claim: Six research desks name the July US inflation releases as the key upcoming data event this window.

July CPI and PPI inflation data releases
